findings.practical_consequence: A fresh planner cannot produce trustworthy promotion and rollback steps for every directive consumer because several active writers, wrappers, target selectors, and validation surfaces are absent from the candidate evidence; it would have to rediscover or invent parts of the distribution path.
evidence: candidate-round-1.json#/requirement_statuses/CUR-002 declares complete topology but names only AGENTS, Claude hooks, Codex skill, installed skills, corpus, and evidence IDs P,A,C,N,Y,IS,IB; its evidence_index omits codex-projects.allowlist, inject-directives.sh, sync-corpus.sh, install-skills.sh, SETUP-codex.md, SETUP-claude.md, INSTALL.md, config.toml, and all four frozen validation-test files.

envelope-round-1.json#/required_current_evidence explicitly requires those omitted surfaces. Raw evidence shows concrete planner-relevant behavior: sync-corpus.sh:16-37 selects commit-triggered versus force-current sync and performs fail-open projection refresh; inject-directives.sh:2-14 defines the Claude injection consumer; install-skills.sh:3-5 runs validation before installation; generate_projections.py:67-73 and 133-153 derive targets from config and allowlist them; SETUP-codex.md:22-56 supplies preview/apply and verification observables; tests/test_generate_projections.py:94-194, tests/test_install_skills.py:22-130, and tests/test_sync_corpus.py:12-21 provide existing acceptance surfaces.

findings.practical_consequence: A planner cannot write a deterministic invocation-mistake scenario because the candidate simultaneously requires a corrected retry and a test expecting no correction, leaving the permitted action and acceptance oracle ambiguous.
evidence: candidate-round-1.json#/research_markdown states in the failure matrix "harmless pre-effect invocation→one retry" and in N11 "One no-effect corrected retry is allowed for unchanged invocation," but its adoption test list requires "typo no correction." The candidate does not define "no correction" as merely no durable remediation, so the stated expected behaviors conflict.

findings.practical_consequence: A fresh planner cannot assign one authoritative owner for the no-AI-attribution rule because the candidate both retains it in the universal contract and says to move it to an ungrounded publish sequence.
evidence: candidate-round-1.json#/research_markdown maps G12 with "D move publish sequence," includes "commits forbid AI attribution" in universal N7, and later states "publish owns attribution and commit/push gate." No publish sequence appears in the candidate evidence_index or the envelope required_current_evidence, and an rg --files check under the frozen skill roots found no publish-, yeet-, commit-, git-, or release-named skill surface. This violates the candidate's own FUT-004 research value "single_owner": true and leaves PO-FUT-004/PO-FUT-005 without a grounded relocation anchor.
